Hello [USER] , thank you for filing this ticket!

It would be very helpful to get some more clarification on what you're experiencing. It sounds like there are 2 things here, so I will break it into sections. For both of these scenarios, providing minimal repros would be very appreciated!

---------------

1. "The update to v1.44.0 and v1.44.1 appears to significantly slower. Especially the sidebar shows far more flicker and higher load times then before?"

Can you be more specific about "sidebar showing far more flicker?" This is visual flicker that happens when? On page load? When interacting with the sidebar? When expanding/collapsing the sidebar?

When it comes to higher load time, can you narrow this down? Is this slower backend response times? Slower render times? 
Is this happening when developing locally? Or when it's deployed somewhere? There are a lot of variables when it comes to performance!

One thing that could be helpful for debugging frontend performance is to get [a Performance Trace using Chrome Devtools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance#record). This produces a trace .json file. You could also get traces for different versions of Streamlit 1.43 vs 1.44 and compare them. If you could get performance traces for these scenarios and share them with us, that would be great!

---------------

2. "Also, with the new release I'm seeing a "Page cannot to be found" dialog/error"

There are a number of different places where an error in this vein could show up in Streamlit. Are you able to create a minimal repro of this error? With a minimal repo, are you able to validate that it works in previous versions of Streamlit? That will help us in pinpointing any possible issues.

Thanks again!

[USER] I'm sorry for taking so long to answer but I'm really swamped. The "Page cannot to be found" is resolved, it was an internal issue but only showed with the new release. Also, the fact that streamlit did not indicate what page was missing didn't make things easier but there's always the debugger. 

As for the rendering and sidebar. I'm using a multi-page app and orchestrate the menu myself using st.page_link(...). It worked great so far and is much cleaner.

Starting with v1.41.0 and also in v1.41.1 the entire sidebar seems to always get reloaded any time one moves from one menu entrance to the next. This causes visual flickering and is not great for the UX, to say the least.

In initially I thought it is cause by my modifications using st.markdown(...)

Thank you for the additional info [USER]! I synced with the team on this and it seems like the sidebar visual flicker is a known issue with the refactoring that was done to align the implementation details of our approaches to building Multipage apps.

If you are attempting to orchestra the menu yourself, our recommendation is to utilize `st.navigation` with `position="hidden"` on the main file, and then manually add the `st.page_link` commands into the Sidebar. Something like this should prevent the sidebar from flickering in this case:

```python
pg = st.navigation(
    [
        "pages/page_1.py",
        "pages/page_2.py",
    ],
    position="hidden",
)

pg.run()

with st.sidebar:
    st.page_link("pages/page_1.py", label="Page 1")
    st.page_link("pages/page_2.py", label="Page 2")
```

[USER], thanks for the update on the topic. Trouble is, I don't know how to use this within my context. Let me try to explain my use case, in hope you can help solve it. The flickering sounds like not much, but I'm getting a lot of heat for it. All my pages call make_sidebar() based on login status. I can't see why this would cause flickering? Here's some more detail: I created a `navigation.py` with logic to load pages from a .yaml file, e.g. ` sections: - name: "Home" expanded: true icon: ":material/home_app_logo:" pages: - path: "pages/0_Main_Page.py" label: "Home" icon: ":material/manage_search:" - path: "pages/1_Manage_Classes.py" label: "Manage Classes" icon: ":material/school:" - path: "pages/2_Start_Class.py" label: "Start Class" icon: ":material/record_voice_over:" ` the `load_entity_navigation` function reads the yaml. within that file I have a function that set's the sidebar. The main logic is: ` def make_sidebar(sidebar_state=st.session_state.get("initial_sidebar_state", "auto")): with st.sidebar: if st.session_state.get("login_status", False): st.logo( image=f"{config.LOGO_PATH}", size="large", link=f"{config.LOGO_LINK}", icon_image=f"{config.LOGO_PATH_SMALL}", ) st.markdown( f"""

Active user: {st.session_state["userinfo"]["preferred_username"]} ({st.session_state["userinfo"]["entity_org"]})

""", unsafe_allow_html=True, ) # Check if YAML configuration exists for this entity entity_config = None if st.session_state.login_user: entity_config = load_entity_navigation(st.session_state.login_user) ...... elif get_current_page_name() != "Home": # If anyone tries to access a secret page without being logged in, redirect them to the login page st.switch_page("gui/Home.py") ` I adjusted `get_current_page_name` after your refactoring to retrieve the proper name of the current page. ` from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner import get_script_run_ctx # def get_current_page_name(): ctx = get_script_run_ctx() # we can local info like timezone froom ctx object. if ctx is None: raise RuntimeError("Couldn't get script context") page_name = Path(ctx.main_script_path).stem # logger.info(f"Current page name: {page_name}") return page_name ` I am using st.page_link e.g. ` def make_sidebar(sidebar_state=st.session_state.get("initial_sidebar_state", "auto")): # Render pages in this section for page in section.get("pages", []): st.page_link( page["path"], label=page.get("label", os.path.basename(page["path"])), icon=page.get("icon", ""), ) ` __________________________________________ I love your product, but frankly, the navigation concept is a total mess and feels unsupported. Every reasonable app requires more sophisticated menu management than what is available.
Any news on this. My perfectly fine app now flickers like a bad website from the '90th. What happened?
